title: Isandro and the Regiment
premise: In the river city of Vellamont, 1792, Felix Eastwick works her late father's type-cutting bench in a print shop whose owner quietly prints seditious pamphlets. When the winter bridge closes and a dying courier hides a ledger of the magistrate's massacres inside a case of type, Felix inherits both the evidence and the danger. Guided by Isandro, a disgraced soldier turned ferryman's son, she must carry the ledger past three checkpoints before New Year's, when an amnesty burns all pending charges. She succeeds at terrible cost: Isandro takes her place at the final checkpoint and is arrested under her name, and Felix must choose between publishing the truth that frees a city and confessing to save him.
about_author: Juniper Vasquez is a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring eighteenth-century print shops across the Rhine valley. Her novels are known for their tactile detail and their stubborn belief that ordinary hands move history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the Eastwick print shop, Felix cuts punches by lamplight while revolution mutters in the streets outside. Establishes her grief for her father, her invisibility as a woman in the trade, and her fierce competence. Emotional beat: quiet pride shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: Pamphlets After Hours
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She discovers master printer Corvel printing anonymous broadsides naming Magistrate Halden's massacres. He swears her to silence; she agrees but keeps a proof sheet hidden in her apron. Emotional beat: complicity and the first thrill of choosing a side.

chapters.title: The Man on the Ice
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A courier crosses the freezing river against orders and collapses on the far bank, pursued. Isandro, who ferries contraband to feed his sister, recognizes the man carrying something wrapped in oilcloth. Emotional beat: wary compassion hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Case of Type
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The dying courier reaches the print shop and dies with his hand on a type case. Felix opens it and finds the ledger sewn beneath the sorts—names, dates, orders signed by Halden himself. Emotional beat: horror and the sudden weight of inheritance.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Soldiers seal the bridge for the season; the city becomes a trap. Corvel urges burning the ledger; Felix refuses—the dead courier's last words named a publisher beyond the river. Emotional beat: claustrophobia sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Isandro of the Ferry Stairs
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro comes to the shop seeking payment for guiding the courier and finds Felix guarding the case like a wolf over a kill. They strike a wary bargain: he knows the checkpoints; she knows how to hide paper in plain sight. Emotional beat: grudging mutual respect.

chapters.title: Hiding Truth Among Letters
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Using her father's techniques, Felix recasts the ledger's pages as printer's galleys of harmless almanac verse, each line encoding testimony. First rehearsal run nearly caught by a patrol. Emotional beat: craft as courage.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Customhouse
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Disguised as a widow shipping funeral goods, Felix passes the customhouse—but a clerk recognizes Corvel's watermark on her wrapping. Isandro creates a diversion that costs him a beating. Emotional beat: terror braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Corvel's POV. Under interrogation threats, Corvel's apprentice Betto betrays the shop's secrets to Halden's men. Corvel, complicit for years, must decide whether to protect Felix or himself. Emotional beat: cowardice curdling into shame.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro's sister Livia begs him to stop; Halden has promised clemency to informers. He lies to her face for the first time. Flashback to his discharge from the regiment after refusing an order to fire on strikers. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made personal.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Soldiers ransack the print shop. Felix watches her father's punches scattered, the presses defaced, while the disguised galleys sit in plain view on the composing stone—and pass inspection unread. Corvel is taken. Emotional beat: violation, then stunned survival.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Toll Gate
chapters.summary: Both POVs. With Corvel imprisoned, Felix travels alone as a typesetter hired for a country job. At the toll gate an officer—who once worked under her father—lingers over her papers. Isandro's staged cart accident pulls the guards away. Emotional beat: the debt between them deepening into trust.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A blizzard strands them in a roadside inn full of refugees from Halden's purges. Listening to their stories, Felix understands the ledger isn't paper—it's them. She and Isandro speak honestly for the first time. Emotional beat: tenderness amid ruin.

chapters.title: Livia's Choice
chapters.summary: Livia's POV. Livia discovers her brother's role and faces her own bargain with Halden's men. Instead of informing, she sends Felix a warning via laundry mark: Betto knows the route. Emotional beat: a sister choosing blood over safety.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Millrace
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Betto leads soldiers to intercept them at the frozen millrace. In the fight the almanac galleys scatter across the ice; Felix and Isandro crawl gathering pages under musket fire. Isandro is wounded. Emotional beat: desperation, sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Confession of Corvel
chapters.summary: Corvel's POV. In prison, Corvel bargains: he will authenticate the ledger publicly if Felix gets his confession out. His cellmate smuggles it to Felix folded inside a psalm. Emotional beat: a compromised man buying back his soul too late to save himself.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The River Fort
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The final checkpoint before the publisher's press. Halden himself inspects travelers, holding a warrant for 'the Eastwick girl.' Isandro volunteers to walk through wearing her coat and carrying a decoy case. Emotional beat: love expressed as self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. On New Year's Eve the amnesty voids old charges—including Isandro's arrest under her name, now converted to sedition. Felix reaches the press as bells ring midnight; the true ledger goes to the compositor. But amnesty also shields Halden. Emotional beat: triumph undercut by injustice.

chapters.title: Print It Anyway
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The publisher hesitates—amnesty makes prosecution impossible, so why risk scandal? Felix sets the type herself, page by page, through the night, arguing that law's forgiveness is not truth's verdict. Emotional beat: vocation as weapon.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The pamphlet floods Vellamont. Crowds read names aloud at the bridge; soldiers refuse to disperse them; Halden resigns under public weight though untouched by courts. Livia testifies about Betto. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, imperfect and real.

chapters.title: Her Name in the Case
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Released by amnesty, Isandro returns to find Felix rehanging her father's punches, having signed the pamphlet 'cut by F. Eastwick.' He brings bread and his sister's blessing. Emotional beat: two people rebuilt around shared truth.

chapters.title: First Impressions
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, epilogue. Spring: the bridge reopens. The shop prints under new ownership—Felix's—with Isandro running deliveries past the checkpoints that no longer matter. She casts a new punch bearing no name but her own. Emotional beat: inheritance claimed, future begun.
